newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM subsidiary up for sale.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM subsidiary up for sale.

text.p: The Zambia Privatisation Agency (ZPA) has put up for sale the Mpelembe Drilling Company, a Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) subsidiary, under an on-going national privatisation programme.
"We are offering up to 80 percent shares in Mpelembe Drilling Company. The company is the only contract mining company in Zambia," the spokesman said.

The company's activities include primary and development mining works, underground civil construction, mechanical and electric installation work, exploratory drilling, water wells, borehole drilling and installations and engineering.

Mpelembe's biggest customer ZCCM accounted for 100 percent of its contract mining activities in Luanshya, Nkana, Konkola, Mufulira and Nampundwe mines over the past two years. The company controls about 80 percent of all contracts awarded by ZCCM in other areas.
In 1995-96 Mpelembe, located in the northern town of Luanshya, recorded a turnover of $7.4 million with profit before tax at $730,000.
Current major contracts expected to continue over the next year range between $6 million and $7 million.
The company has 1,483 permanent employees and 1,147 contract staff.
